scope: Independent review of stateless OAuth source repair, guarded installer and fourteen native regressions authored by fixture_source_review agent; final response-commit delta and retained Spring source inspected.

findings.discovered_by: fixture_source_review agent after initial source review
findings.summary: Spring session repository response-commit wrapper may save the current bearer/empty request context before the OAuth filter finally restores the original browser context.
findings.impact: An existing browser session can be transiently overwritten or removed, potentially affecting a concurrent request despite final restoration.
findings.required_resolution: Prevent persistence of the entire request-scoped context at every save point; add native tests with actual HttpSessionSecurityContextRepository commit wrapper asserting session content before filter finally.
findings.resolution: A directly @Transient-annotated SecurityContextImpl subclass is installed only for each opt-in service request. The retained Spring repository checks this annotation before both direct and response-commit saves, preventing session replacement/removal before the original browser context is restored in finally.

regression_baseline.scope: Same final fourteen-test fixture compiled separately against untouched native-final01 classes; actual Spring session repository and response wrapper expose removal/replacement during the filter chain before finally.

result: No unresolved material source finding in this bounded review. SR-01 reproduced against the prior compiled candidate and resolved by the final transient context source with both response-commit regressions passing; final configured WAR HTTP evidence remains separately required.
checks: Explicit default-false option survives serialized clone; historical branch remains default.
Fresh service SecurityContext ignores browser session identity and finally restores original context for the surrounding persistence filter.
Current bearer token selects the cache key; absent token does not use a custom-session cookie.
Direct native token verification avoids the session-scoped OAuth template; verified request attributes and configured role resolution remain.
Configured UserGroupService requires a known enabled user in opt-in mode; reserved root principal no longer bypasses configured roles.
Native tests assert cookie-only and mismatched-bearer denial, no session/template use, configured authorities, cache reuse/invalidation/expiry, and context restoration on downstream exception.
Guarded helper validates all exact source, output, replacement-count and native fixture identities before source writes.

Both native response-commit regressions use the actual Spring HttpSessionSecurityContextRepository and wrapped response, asserting browser session identity during sendError/flushBuffer before filter finally; both fail on prior source and pass on final source.
limitations: Native stateless tests use mocked token/user/role services, real native filter/role resolution/cache and actual Spring session repository response wrapper; they supplement the real configured WAR HTTP matrix.
Human security review, canonical policy, browser SSO and production/release acceptance remain separate.
